title: Arrays and a Span preview
hook: An array is a CLR object with a fixed Length and O(1) indexing. Span<T> is a view over memory, not a collection you store on a class. Name Span here; the rules live in module 17.

sections.heading: Arrays are objects with a length
sections.prose: int[] scores = new int[3]; allocates a reference-type array on the heap (unless stackalloc, which is not an array object). Length never changes. You can write scores[i]; going past Length throws IndexOutOfRangeException. Rectangular arrays (int[,]) and jagged arrays (int[][]) are different types — jagged is an array of arrays and is what you actually ship. Arrays implement IList<T> but throw on Add. SZ arrays (single-dimension, zero-based) are the fast path the JIT special-cases. An SQS ReceiveMessage result you immediately map to Message[] is fine when the batch size is capped (10 is the SQS classic). Do not use an array as an append buffer; that is List<T>.

snippets.label: Fixed batch as array
snippets.explanation: Once the receive call returns, the batch is a closed set. Array matches that. A later retry is a new receive, a new array.

sections.heading: Array covariance is a loaded gun
sections.prose: string[] names = ["a"]; object[] boxed = names; compiles because arrays are covariant. boxed[0] = 3; compiles as object and throws ArrayTypeMismatchException at run time. Generic List<string> does not allow this — that is a reason generics exist (module 09). Mention covariance of arrays in interviews so you can contrast it with IEnumerable<out T> later.

sections.heading: Span<T> is a preview, not this module
sections.prose: Span<T> and ReadOnlySpan<T> let you slice an array, stack memory, or unmanaged memory without copying. Collection expressions can target Span<string> weekDays = ["Sun", "Mon"];. Span is a ref struct: it cannot live on the heap, cannot be a field of a class, cannot be used in async methods without careful scoping. Those constraints, slicing, and performance belong in module 17 (Span, unsafe, interop). Here you only need the sentence: if the interviewer says “zero-copy slice of the CSV line,” you answer Span<T>, then you do not fake a Span-based parser in this chapter.

interviewTakeaways: Arrays have fixed Length; indexing is O(1); they are reference types.
Array covariance can throw ArrayTypeMismatchException; List<T> does not.
Span<T> is a ref-struct view — full treatment is module 17.
commonPitfalls: Calling Add on an array typed as IList<T> and being surprised by NotSupportedException.
Using object[] as a heterogeneous bag and hitting array covariance bugs.
Trying to store Span<T> on a worker class field — illegal; wait for module 17 to see why.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS arrays grow. C# arrays do not. JS Array is closer to List<T> than to T[].

jsTsCorrelations.concept: T[] vs readonly T[] vs tuple
jsTsCorrelations.note: TS T[] is a growable JS array at run time. C# T[] is fixed. TS tuples are closer in intent to a fixed array but still JS arrays.
